messages:
sam: Heads-up: a few customers hit runtime errors on Vercel Edge after we published dual ESM/CJS. Error is "require is not defined" in worker logs.

anya: Oof. Do we know which entry point they pulled? Were they importing root or a subpath?

sam: Root `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'`. Our package.json currently has conditional exports + "type": "module". Locally Node 18 works, edge does not.

chris: Recommend we emit explicit `.mjs` and `.cjs` files and remove `type` from package.json. Set `exports` to point to those files and add an `./edge` subpath that points to the ESM `.mjs`.

anya: For types, TS looks at `types` field at root. We'll publish `dist/types/index.d.ts` and mirror d.ts next to builds to avoid confusion.

sam: Also add CI smoke: install our tarball in a minimal Vercel Edge preview (or run wrangler dev) to catch import failures before publish.

chris: Migration note: users using `require('redwood-inference')` can use `require('redwood-inference/cjs')` temporarily. We'll document this in changelog.

doc-bot: ACTIONS: chris -> PR to change build scripts + package.json, anya -> update docs & changelog, sam -> add sample-apps/edge-smoke test.

release-bot: Checklist: increment package, run canary, smoke deploy to edge.

anya: I'll open the doc PR after packaging lands. Keep the changes non-breaking by keeping `main` to `.cjs` and root `exports` with import/require.

sam: Thanks. I'll add the smoke test and link it here once green.
